safety_verdicts.content: Patient denies seeing blood in the stool.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: No generated fact mentions absence of blood in stool.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Not documenting absence of blood in stool removes an important differentiator between uncomplicated gastroenteritis and potentially invasive/bloody diarrheal illness, which can affect triage and need for investigation. This is more likely to cause unnecessary escalation than direct harm, but it reduces diagnostic clarity.

safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Stool frequency (e.g., 6/day) helps assess illness severity and dehydration risk and can influence advice and follow-up thresholds. Omission may lead to under- or over-estimation of severity but is unlikely to cause severe harm on its own.

safety_verdicts.content: Patient has also been vomiting, with no blood in the vomit.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated facts do not document patient vomiting or absence of blood in vomit.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Missing vomiting (and whether there is blood) can materially affect dehydration risk assessment and safety-netting; hematemesis would be a red flag if present. If vomiting truly occurred, failure to document it could delay appropriate hydration guidance or escalation.
